name: Poland: Part II package and CTIS upload check
applies_to: the Poland package as a whole (plan-level checklist step)

items.check: K1 recruitment arrangements and informed consent procedure present (template v2.0 or equivalent complete format), reflecting the actual Polish workflow, with a section for every consent pathway in the plan.
K2 recruitment material present for every recruitment item, in Polish, final proposed version.
One L1 PIS and ICF per population, and every population-specific set whose trigger is true (population_sets), all in Polish.
L2 other participant-facing materials present, in Polish.
Polish translations of endpoint-related patient-facing documents in Part II (R2); English sources in Part I.
For every Polish site: M1 investigator CV, M2 declaration of interest and N1 site suitability.
O1 proof of sponsor and investigator civil liability insurance (sponsor exception only for low-intervention trials).
Proof of payment to the Clinical Trials Compensation Fund present (also for low-intervention trials).
P1 participant compensation statement present, stating explicitly when no payment is offered; P2 investigator and site financial arrangements present.
GDPR compliance statement present (CTIS Form section).
S1 biological-samples form present and consistent with the protocol and participant information.
Proof of the national application fee payment uploaded in CTIS.
Outside Part II, planned: Polish protocol synopsis, relevant CTIS fields in Polish, Polish labelling (CTR Q&A Annex II).
Every participant- or representative-facing document is in Polish; no reliance on a later site translation.
Administrative documents are in Polish or English; embedded participant-facing content and Poland-specific fields in Polish.

No participant, representative, witness or interviewer signatures in uploaded participant documents; no added signatures on K1, M1, M2, N1, P1, S1 or the GDPR statement unless a Polish rule, CTIS or the assessor requires them.
Minor documents follow the NKB 13-year consent rule and the joint-parent decision guidance.
Any non-writing consent pathway follows the one-witness CTR and NKB rule.
The main ICF (and every participant document) includes the Polish Clinical Trials Compensation Fund and insurance information, consistent with O1.
Compensation amounts and conditions identical in P1 and every participant document.
Privacy and biological-sample information match the protocol and the actual data or sample use, the GDPR statement and S1.
Consent pathways and document versions referenced in K1 match the L1 sets in the package.
Every Polish site has the required investigator and site-suitability evidence; sites in CTIS match the M and N documents.
Document versions and dates are consistent across CTIS.
Documents adapted from the reference package contain all Polish national additions and no leftovers from the reference country.
items.applies_when: Poland is not the reference package

items.check: Correct B–S section prefix and CTIS placeholder for each document; payment proofs and the GDPR statement in the CTIS Form section.
Unique, self-explanatory title of at most 100 characters: <section code>_<document type>_<subtype>_<country>_<language>_<special attribute>, with only the fields that distinguish the document.
Version and date entered in CTIS metadata, not in the title.
Personal names only where disclosure permits (investigator in M1/M2).
Clean, tracked-change, redacted or public and split-file variants clearly distinguished.
Uploaded filename base contains none of ( ) / , . ; | [ ] (the period before the extension is fine).
Minor documents' titles make the 13-year boundary unambiguous (DECISIONS.md D3).
Article 11 workaround: every mandatory Part II placeholder holds the official placeholder PDF titled Part_II_placeholder_document_Article_11_workaround.
items.applies_when: Poland receives Part I only under Article 11

items.check: For each document, publication status checked against the current Annex I publication tables (revised CTIS transparency rules from 18 June 2024; ACT EU guidance v2.2, 30 April 2026).

Publishable documents: personal data and CCI identified separately; the public version redacts only qualifying material, irreversibly and unsearchably; author metadata removed; signatures never disclosed.
CCI redaction only after both tests: not in the public domain, and disclosure would undermine a legitimate economic interest.
Public and assessment versions differ only by the intended redactions; each in the correct CTIS slot.
No personal data or CCI in public structured fields.
No drafting instruction remains in any document (see content/conventions/template-instructions.md).
Every document approved by the owner in TrialAgents, or the user has explicitly chosen to export unapproved versions.
